editorial:
If you love spy movies with a sense of humor, this one is a fun ride. Jason Statham plays Orson Fortune, a tough special agent who gets pulled into a mission to stop a dangerous new weapons tech from being sold. To pull it off, his team recruits Danny Francesco, a famous Hollywood movie star played by Josh Hartnett, who gets way more than he bargained for. Aubrey Plaza and Hugh Grant round out a great cast, and the whole thing has that slick, fast-talking Guy Ritchie energy. The banter between the characters keeps things light even when the stakes are high, and the globe-trotting locations look gorgeous on screen.

The action scenes are well put together, with plenty of shootouts, chases, and clever cons. Statham does what he does best, and Plaza steals almost every scene she is in. On the downside, the plot can feel a little busy at times, and some jokes land better than others. Still, if you want a breezy action thriller for a weekend night, this delivers. It is a great pick for fans of spy comedies and action lovers.
endingExplained: In the final act, Orson and his team track down the weapons deal and discover that Hugh Grant's character, Greg Simmonds, is the one brokering the sale. Danny Francesco uses his acting skills to help trick the bad guys during a tense undercover operation. The team manages to stop the weapons from changing hands and takes down the villains. In the end, Orson and his crew walk away victorious, with Danny heading back to Hollywood a little wiser and a lot more shaken. The movie closes on a light note, hinting that Orson's team will be back for another mission soon.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves spy comedies and action thrillers.
